## How to use this starter

unfinished starter can render. Replace each TODO, remove that option, and render
again. A successful render of the untouched starter is not completion.

## Supplied synthetic data and helpers

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

# Synthetic teaching data for BIOS 6301. Not real patients.
set.seed(6301)
n <- 60
trial <- data.frame(
  id        = sprintf("P%03d", 1:n),
  arm       = rep(c("Placebo", "Treatment"), each = n / 2),
  site      = sample(1:4, n, replace = TRUE),
  age       = round(rnorm(n, 61, 9)),
  sex       = sample(c("F", "M"), n, replace = TRUE),
  weight_kg = round(rnorm(n, 82, 15), 1),
  sbp_0     = round(rnorm(n, 148, 14)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
trial$sbp_12 <- round(trial$sbp_0 -
  ifelse(trial$arm == "Treatment", rnorm(n, 14, 8), rnorm(n, 3, 8)))

# Repeated-measures version of the same cohort, for the resampling-unit demo:
# three visits per patient, a large patient-level random intercept (SD 12) and
# small within-patient noise (SD 4). Nothing is "broken" here — the data are
# simply clustered, which is what makes the row bootstrap wrong.
set.seed(2024)
patient_effect <- rnorm(n, 0, 12)
trial_long <- data.frame(
  id   = rep(trial$id, each = 3),
  arm  = rep(trial$arm, each = 3),
  week = rep(c(4, 8, 12), times = n),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
trial_long$sbp <- round(140 + rep(patient_effect, each = 3) +
  ifelse(trial_long$arm == "Treatment", -10, 0) + rnorm(n * 3, 0, 4))

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 15))
gold <- "#CFAE70"

mean_diff <- function(data) {
  mean(data$sbp_12[data$arm == "Treatment"]) -
    mean(data$sbp_12[data$arm == "Placebo"])
}
```

## Start with the project question

We have one dataset. Choose the repeated operation from the question:

| Question | Method | Output |
|---|---|---|
| How uncertain is an estimate? | Bootstrap participants | SE and interval |
| Is the observed difference surprising under a specified null? | Permute allowed assignments | p-value |

The melanoma and promotion-decision projects illustrate these two questions.
This lab uses a synthetic cohort of 60 participants. Cross-validation is taught
with regression models in Session 16.


## 1. Bootstrap within arms

Estimate the Treatment-minus-Placebo mean difference in 12-week SBP. Bootstrap participants within each arm. Report bootstrap SE and a percentile interval, and compare the SE with Welch. Basic intervals, bias, and three-seed stability comparisons are optional follow-up.

## 2. Permutation tests

For a completely randomized design under the sharp null, permute arm labels, retain 999 statistics, and compute the adjusted two-sided p-value. Report its resolution. The binomial tail-probability interval and exact-enumeration demonstration below are optional follow-up.

```{r, eval=FALSE}

# Exact enumeration includes the observed assignment; no +1 correction is needed there.
```

Interpret the result and state its limitations.

### Supplied exact-enumeration demonstration

```{r}
small <- trial[c(1:4, 31:34), ]
assignment <- combn(8, 4)
exact_stat <- apply(assignment, 2, function(i)
  mean(small$sbp_12[i]) - mean(small$sbp_12[-i]))
stopifnot(length(exact_stat) == 70L)
mean(abs(exact_stat) >= abs(mean_diff(small)))
```

## Paired-data follow-up

For treatment-arm participants, calculate follow-up minus baseline SBP. Bootstrap
these paired changes and report the mean, SE, and percentile interval. Explain why
this does not estimate a causal treatment effect, why independent resampling of the
two visits is inappropriate, and why time labels cannot automatically be permuted.
